subject: Next steps & decision criteria for ClearWave inference (latency / SLA / procurement)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@clearwave.ai>, Tom Harris <tharris@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:14:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + ask: latency targets, buyers, procurement path

Thanks for the conversation today — good alignment and a lot to work with. Quick recap and three asks so we can update the MAP and lock timelines: 

Recap (high level)
- ClearWave use case: customer support summarization + real-time reranking for help center results (primary production goal).
- Preferred initial volume: ~50k queries/day for first 6 months, ramp to 200k/day.
- Security posture: SOC 2 required, likely internal audit in H1 once in prod.

Asks / open items (please confirm):
1) Economic buyer / procurement owner: who signs the SOW and handles budget approval? (You mentioned Janet Lee — can we get her email and preferred procurement contact?)
2) Security & legal: who will own the security questionnaire and evidence (SOC 2 report + data retention policy)? Any additional regulatory constraints or data residency needs?
3) Decision criteria — please confirm numeric targets we should optimize for:
   - Latency SLO: p95 target for 512-token responses (is 120ms acceptable, or do you need lower?)
   - Cost guardrail: target cost per 1M tokens or equivalent monthly spend cap for the first 6 months?
   - Deployment mode: preference between Hosted (fast POC) vs Dedicated reserved GPU pools vs Private (VPC / on-prem) for production.

Attached: redwood-sla-options.pdf (SLA tiers + latency profiles) and a draft mutual-action-plan.xlsx to populate names/times.

Proposed next steps
- You confirm the three asks above by EOD Thu (11/05) so we can finalize a MAP and scope a POC that matches your latency/cost targets.
- We can provision a hosted POC within 2 business days after signature of the NDA; Dedicated sizing estimate follows after workload traces.

Thanks — I’ll sync the MAP with Soojin and Monica once we get your answers.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.inference
From: Tom Harris <tharris@clearwave.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>, Olivia Grant <olivia@clearwave.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: latency targets, buyers, procurement path

Thanks Rafael — good summary. A few clarifications on our side so you can update the MAP: 

1) Economic buyer / procurement
- Economic buyer: Janet Lee, CFO (janet.lee@clearwave.ai). She owns budget sign-off for platform spend > $50k/month.
- Procurement contact for contracts: procurement@clearwave.ai (they handle NDAs and SOW redlines).

2) Security / compliance
- Security owner: me (Tom Harris, Head of Infrastructure) for technical evidence, and Legal will lead contract-level concerns. SOC 2 Type II in scope; we will need access to your SOC reports and an explicit data retention policy for inference logs (we prefer 90 days retention for logs and customer content purge on request).

3) Decision criteria (engineering asks)
- Latency: target p95 <= 120ms for 512-token typical responses — lower would be great but not mandatory for phase 1.
- Cost: target operational spend ~ $25k-$40k/month initially (rough cap for first 6 months). If you can show projected per-1M token cost that keeps us inside that cap at expected volumes, that will help.
- Deployment: we prefer Hosted for POC, then Dedicated reserved capacity for production (data isolation and predictable throughput). Private/on-prem is a later-stage ask only if compliance requires it.

Timeline
- Procurement timeline: procurement team typically requires 2-3 weeks for NDA/SOW review after pricing is agreed.
- Decision window: Janet plans to make a commit by end of November if the POC meets latency and cost expectations.

Tom
Tom Harris
Head of Infrastructure | ClearWave
tharris@clearwave.ai

Subject: Re: Recap + ask: latency targets, buyers, procurement path

Appreciate the detail, Tom. A few technical notes and an outline of options we can present in the MAP: 

Technical clarifications
- The p95 <= 120ms ask for 512-token responses is achievable on Dedicated for the expected QPS with conservative batching disabled for low-latency paths; Hosted POC will likely be within 120–180ms p95 depending on load during the window. We’ll instrument traces during POC to give you measured p95 performance.
- Caching/prefix-KV can reduce observed latencies for repeated contexts; worth identifying if many queries share prefixes.

Deployment options for MAP (recommended path)
1) Short POC: Hosted (2–4 weeks) — quick to provision, will validate latency and output quality.
2) Staging: Small Dedicated pool (1–2 reserved GPUs) — target p95 <= 120ms at expected traffic and will give more realistic cost forecasts.
3) Production: Dedicated reserved capacity with autoscaling + cross-region fallback (if you need DR). Private only if Legal requires custody of keys/data.

SLA options
- We have three SLA tiers (see attached redwood-sla-options.pdf): Standard (99.9% uptime, best-effort latency), Business (99.95%, latency objectives with credits), and Enterprise (99.99%, custom latency SLOs and incident response). For your p95 target we recommend Business tier during production.

Questions for your team
- Can you share a small sample of typical prompt sizes and distribution (we only need token-length histogram, not content)?
- Any regional constraints (must keep traffic in us-east-1 / us-west-2 / eu-west-1)?

I’ll draft the MAP rows for POC + staging + production and tag owners (Janet for budget, Tom for security, procurement@clearwave.ai for contracts).

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.inference
